processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds were successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast, the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10×50×130 mm³-sized blocks were hot rolled at 1100 °C into 2±0.1 mm-thick and ~500-mm-long sheets.
Sheets were reheated to 1100 °C and water quenched.

processing_steps.method: cutting perpendicular to the rolling direction
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments with dimensions 2×60×55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
Homogenization was performed at 1100 °C for 2 h under Ar, followed by water quenching.
No subsequent aging was applied; this sample corresponds to the as-homogenized (0 h aging) reference condition.
Scales were removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized single-phase austenitic microstructure with some retained microsegregations of Mn.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Mechanical response relative to the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy in the as-homogenized state (360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE): without aging, Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al shows a similar mechanical response, with only a minor change in YS (increase), UTS, and TE (decrease).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; values are averages of three measurements.
characterization_methods.purpose: Mechanical screening of yield strength (YS), ultimate tensile strength (UTS), and total elongation (TE).
characterization_methods.key_findings: As-homogenized Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al YS rises to about the 500 MPa line at 8Al (Fig. 3a).

characterization_methods.purpose: Mechanical screening of hardness across RAP sample conditions.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm.
Cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction by grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques.
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructure characterization (recrystallization, grain size, segregation, defects).
characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; hot rolling and water quenching resulted in a fully recrystallized microstructure with a grain size of ~20 µm and some retained microsegregations of Mn.

unmapped_findings: Without aging, the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al alloy shows a mechanical response similar to that of the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy (as-homogenized: 360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE), with only a minor change in YS (increase), UTS, and TE (decrease) (b0023, b0024).
Aging Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al for 24 h further increases YS, UTS, and hardness to levels twice as high as in the as-homogenized state and drastically reduces ductility (b0024).
Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al is the material with the highest Al content and lowest density in the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl RAP set (b0024).

In the as-homogenized/naturally aged state, Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al is a single-phase austenitic TWIP (SIMPLEX) steel, with dislocation-based strain hardening followed by mechanical twinning as the primary mechanism (b0031).
